text:
sam: Heads-up — we've been seeing a bunch of duplicate traces coming from the edge proxies when connectivity flaps. duplicates show up as separate spans in traces and blow up storage + cost. anyone worked on a resume/idempotency pattern for intermittent shippers?

maya: yes. common pattern: attach a stable "edge-resume-key" per trace + monotonic seq per chunk. ingest side dedupes by key+seq. keeps ordering and avoids re-ingest.

oliver: re: storage growth — dedupe window needs to be bounded. TTL on dedupe cache + tombstones for accepted seq. otherwise global mem grows. we used a 24h window for user-facing traces.

sam: makes sense. how do we generate the resume key without leaking PII for multi-tenant flows?

maya: use trace_id + edge_instance_id hashed with HMAC(key). no raw customer ids. HMAC(secret, trace_id|instance) -> edge-resume-key. then sequence number per chunk.

dana: ingest API needs a header for this: `X-Redwood-Dedupe: <base64(hmac)>; seq=<n>; chunk-start=true|false` so downstream can decide. also add `X-Redwood-Partial: true` when trace incomplete.

ingest-bot: deploy pipeline: telemetry-ingest (canary) succeeded for commit ab12f3 — added dedupe header parsing middleware. :rocket:

oliver: also consider idempotent upload endpoint that accepts `dedupe_id` for whole bundle. If retries happen at transport layer we can return 409 on duplicate. less work for streaming ingestion.

sam: nice. but we also have concern about sampling: if an edge keeps retrying for a sampled-out trace, we don't want to retain dedupe state. how to tie sampling decision?

maya: sample decision should be made at the edge ideally and encoded in the resume header: `sample=0|1|prob=0.01` then ingest can ignore sample=0 footprints and skip dedupe bookkeeping. for probabilistic sampling, annotate with sampling-seed so deterministic replays map same decision.

tia: what about offline buffering on disk? we need local backpressure and eviction policy.

oliver: config we used: ```yaml
telemetry:
  local_buffer:
    max_bytes: 104857600 # 100MB
    max_chunks: 1000
    flush_interval_ms: 5000
    eviction: lru
    persist_path: /var/lib/telemetry/buffer
```

dana: + ensure buffer checkpoints include the last acked seq per resume-key so resume picks up at the right seq. checkpoint file should be appended-only to avoid corruption during crashes.

sam: any infra changes needed on the ingestion pipeline? e.g., dedupe cache storage, tombstone propagation?

maya: we can use sharded Redis with bounded TTL for dedupe slots for hot keys, and fall back to a bloomfilter for best-effort dedupe across cold nodes. tombstones for accepted seqs get a short TTL matching dedupe window.

oliver: for trace reassembly we should add 'partial-bundle' markers and an ordering window. don't rely on arrival order. reassembly buffer keyed by resume-key + highest-seq-seen. drop if gap > N or age > window. N could be 50 for now.

sam: cost angle — keeping dedupe state has cost; would rather have simple heuristics first. Proposal: start with per-edge keyed dedupe (HMAC key rotated monthly), Redis TTL 6h, local buffer 50MB default, and ingest returns 202 on new, 409 on duplicate. evaluate for 2 weeks.

dana: sounds pragmatic. add metrics: `telemetry.dedup_cache_hit`, `telemetry.resumed_traces`, `telemetry.duplicate_rejected` and `telemetry.buffer_evictions`.

ingest-bot: alert: ingest-cluster-2 high-evictions spike at 2025-11-04T09:12:01Z — investigating.

sam: action items: 1) maya to draft API header spec + example curl, 2) oliver to prototype local buffer config and checkpoint format, 3) dana to add metrics to observation plan. follow-up in 48h.

maya: I'll open a short RFC with examples, will include HMAC pseudo-code and curl examples: ```bash
curl -X POST https://ingest.redwood.ai/v1/trace \
  -H "X-Redwood-Dedupe: abc123; seq=1; sample=1" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  --data-binary @trace-chunk.json
```

oliver: I'll mock the buffer and checkpoint file format: single-line JSON entries appended, example: `{"resume_key":"k","seq":12,"acked":true,"offset":4096}`

dana: I'll add metrics + dash and wire alerts for eviction rate and duplicate-reject ratio.

sam: great. thanks all. ping me if you need infra creds for Redis shards.

maya: noted. starting RFC now. :+1:
